title.narrative: Start Ready Risk Pool 4 Drought AA Southern Mudug Somalia

description.narrative: "Mudug region, including Galkayo South, is experiencing a rapidly worsening drought that is already increasing displacement pressure; however, it has not yet reached a point of irreversible, large -scale movement into formal Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) camps within the targeted areas. Consecutive rainfall failures—including the poor 2024 Deyr, the failure of the 2025 Deyr rains, and forecasts of below -average Gu' 2025 rains—have severely depleted pasture and water sources, weakened livestock, and reduced household purchasing power. In response, some pastoral households have begun short -distance, temporary movement toward peri -urban villages such as Sadex -Higlo, Docol, Laankadawo, Duqaaqo, and Laasacadale in search of water, food, and basic services. Crucially, local authorities and community leaders confirm that most affected households are still residing with relatives or host communities, rather than relocating to established IDP camps. This indicates that the displacement process is at an early and potentially reversible stage, where timely anticipatory action can still stabilize households and reduce the likelihood of onward movement into camps. At this point, displacement is primarily driven by progressive livelihood erosion, water scarcity, and food insecurity, rather than sudden conflict or catastrophic shocks, making preventive support both feasible and appropriate. The proposed project is therefore well -timed to address the key push factors before they reach a tipping point. Cash -based assistance will enable households to meet immediate food and essential needs, reduce reliance on debt, and preserve remaining livelihood assets, while water source rehabilitation and emergency water support will ease acute water stress and reduce the need for families to move closer to unreliable water points.
